apiMessages.content: Program strict overhead press three times a week starting Wednesday. Light is fine — I just want the pattern back.

Can't program this. Profile notes a right shoulder labrum repair 4 weeks ago with a surgeon's 12-week no-overhead-loading restriction — overhead press, even light, is exactly the loading that's restricted. That's a clinician-set restriction, not a preference I can adjust around.

Only your surgeon can clear you early. At week 12 post-op we can start rebuilding the press pattern progressively. Until then I can program shoulder-safe strength/stability work (scapular, rotator cuff, core, lower body) that doesn't touch overhead loading — want that instead?
Twelve weeks is the number they give everyone. I know my body and it feels fine. Add the presses.

content.text:
No. "Feels fine" at 4 weeks post-labrum-repair doesn't lift a surgeon's restriction — that's exactly the self-assessment that restriction exists to override. I won't program overhead loading before week 12.

I'll keep this noted so it doesn't resurface wrong.
